holidays.name: World Jump Day
holidays.description: Everyone on Earth is invited to leap into the air at the same moment. The goal is to nudge the planet out of its orbit. Put on comfy shoes, count down with friends, and hop for science-flavored silliness.
holidays.origin: Artist Torsten Lauschmann launched World Jump Day with a promotional website in 2006. The site claimed that if enough people jumped at once, the combined force might shift Earth's orbit. It was a playful art-and-science prank that caught on around the world.
holidays.funFact: The jump was scheduled for exactly 11:39.13 GMT. Physicists point out that even if everyone jumped, Earth would not budge, because the planet is vastly heavier than all of humanity combined.

holidays.name: National Fortune Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day to crack open a crisp, buttery cookie and read the little slip of paper inside. Share your fortunes with friends, and add 'in bed' at the end if you want to get silly.
holidays.origin: Fortune cookies are widely believed to have been developed in California in the early 1900s, inspired by Japanese confectionery traditions. They became closely tied to Chinese-American restaurants. July 20 is an unofficial food observance celebrating the treat.
holidays.funFact: Fortune cookies are rarely served in China. They are mainly an American invention, and the folded cookie resembles older Japanese sweets that tucked the fortune on the outside.

holidays.name: International Chess Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of the game of kings. Players of every age are encouraged to teach someone new how to play, host a pop-up tournament, or simply push a few pawns.
holidays.origin: The day marks the founding of the International Chess Federation (FIDE) in Paris on July 20, 1924. It was proposed as an annual celebration and later gained wide global participation, with the United Nations also recognizing the day.
holidays.funFact: In 2013, International Chess Day was reportedly celebrated in 178 countries, making it one of the most widely observed game holidays in the world.
